He Softfoot was a pandaren rogue and quest giver aligned with the Golden Lotus. He was known to be mute. He was killed in the destruction of the vale caused by Garrosh Hellscream's reawakening of the Sha of Pride. Following his death, he can be encountered in the Siege of Orgrimmar raid as one of The Fallen Protectors. He remains in the scarred area where the Golden Pagoda once stood, tormented and scared at being unable to pass on to the afterlife.

Hayward is a family of Gilnean fishermen, currently consisting of five brothers living at the Hayward Fishery. The brothers have been running the Fishery for years and don't make it to Duskhaven very often, except to trade their fish. The Haywards have been men of the sea for generations. When the populace around Duskhaven were ordered to evacuate to higher ground due to the Forsaken invasion, the Haywards decided to leave by boat rather than being part of the land evacuation. It is unknown what happened to them after the evacuation, as they are never seen again.

Haustvald is a vast stone complex in eastern Stormheim used by the vrykul to perform sacred rituals or ceremonies. The site is located beside the Runewood and the Field of Fallen Kings, carved as it is directly into a large cliff face. Haustvald serves as one of the very few access points to the realm of Helheim, the domain of the Sea-Witch Helya, which can be reached through a portal in the heart of the complex. Haven is the main quest hub in Zereth Mortis. It is the home of the Enlightened and was created out of Progenitor ruins. During the last stages of the war against the Jailer, the settlement came under attack by the Mawsworn, but it was protected by a protective shield and reinforced by Maw Walkers and Covenant armies. Cartel Xy also tried to sabotage Haven. Located in western Zereth Mortis, it is surrounded by Felicitous Glade and the Great Veldt. The Slumbering Vault is located inside Haven, and just outside Haven's walls is the Geometric Cavern.

Healing Touch is a level 26 Restoration druid healing spell. It is the largest direct heal available to the class. It is costly but effective, making it good for delivering large amounts of healing to a target.

A healer is a character whose primary purpose or class role is to heal and protect their allies. Priests, druids, paladins, shamans and monks can all serve as healers. Healers are perhaps the most wanted for a dungeon or a raid. While all party members must work together to succeed, healers have the direct responsibility of keeping every other member of the party alive. Healers must anticipate incoming damage, prioritise the healing of multiple targets, and make split-second decisions using an array of healing options.

Health, health points or hit points (HP) is used to denote the life level for all creatures. When a creature's health falls to zero or below, it dies. The maximum amount of health a player character has is determined by a combination of the character's level and stamina while the health of NPCs is pre-set by the game developers. Certain classes also have buffs which temporarily or permanently increase maximum health, such as a Warrior's Rallying Cry or Stance of the Sturdy Ox. In general, for player characters tanks have the largest amounts of health while healers and damage dealers have less. For NPCs, raid bosses have the largest amounts of health while trash mobs generally have the least.

Healing Wave is a Restoration shaman healing spell. It is a shaman's most mana efficient single-target heal. It doesn't heal for very much, however, and is only really useful at times of lower damage. Its main advantage is that the low mana cost means that you can chain-cast the spell indefinitely.

Hearthglen is a fortified town and former principality in the northern area of the former kingdom of Lordaeron, located north of Andorhal, in an area now known as the Western Plaguelands. It is a sturdy fortress, its walls encircling a town hall, a mage tower, a lumber mill, a blacksmith, stables, a scout tower and a mine besides its keep. The road to the town is called Hearthglen Pass, and a forest near Hearthglen is called the Hearthglen Woods. The town stands out from the rest of the region for its peaceful appearance, although it has not been spared from the attacks of the Scourge. Healadin is a term used by some people for paladins that have specialized their character in healing. They will wear pieces of armour that give advantages to intellect and will have spent talent points deeply into the Holy tree. Healadins are also typical Pocket Healers in battlegrounds, and their plate armor and Divine Shield makes them hard to kill. Prior to the release of The Burning Crusade, the superiority of the healing bonuses to certain pieces of cloth armor, may have led some healadins to wearing cloth. Healing paladins wearing cloth are often referred to as clothadins.

In fact, she is a prisoner of a sort, as the mad furbolgs won't allow her to leave, and because she loves her people, she would rather stay put than hurt any of them. After the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard managed to slip past the furbolgs to speak with Kodian, who was still present in the shrine to continue her duty. The spell has a cooldown that matches the duration, meaning that only one area of rain per shaman can be maintained.

The Heart of the Aspects is a luminous dragon born of the radiant energies of the Dragon Soul artifact. With a glow said to be the equal of a thousand suns, this drakes' blinding light is much like attacking a foe with the sun at your back.

Heart of Fear is one of the three launch raids that opened in World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria. This is the seat of the mantid dominion, and a place where the queen of the mantid currently resides, possessed by the Sha of Fear. The entrance to this raid dungeon is in the base of a large rotting tree structure in the west of the Dread Wastes. Normal mode opened October 30, 2012, first Raid Finder part and Heroic modes opened on November 6, 2012, and second Raid Finder part opened on November 13, 2012. Raid Finder difficulty requires an average item level of 470.
Healer's Wristwraps are a quest reward from The Healing of Shen-zin Su.
Healthy Mushroom is a mushroom located in Ahn'kahet: The Old Kingdom.

The Heart of Jade is east of the central courtyard of Temple of the Jade Serpent in the Jade Forest. In the uninstanced version, Fei, Elder Sage Rain-Zhu, and a Yu'lon Priest are all standing at the entrance. Yu'lon makes her appearance here in The Jade Serpent.
Healiss is a saurok held in a cage in Fire Camp Ruqin in Kun-Lai Summit. He is also found at the Temple of the White Tiger. He is the tank for a P.U.G. participating in the Trial of the White Tiger.

Heart of Destruction is a subzone of the Stonecore. High Priestess Azil and her countless Devout Followers are fought here. This location is where Deathwing recovered and had his new plates fused to his form, as seen in the Cataclysm cinematic, and his old plates can be seen strewn about the area. Of course, the damage to the top of the Temple of Earth begins here. It is called the "World's Heart" by Ozruk.
Headmaster's Will replaces Headmaster's Charge from the pre-Mists of Pandaria version of Scholomance.

Healing per mana (HPM) means how mana efficient a healing spell is.
The Heart of the Thunder King drops at a 100% chance in all difficulties upon the defeat of Lei Shen in the Throne of Thunder while on the eponymous quest Heart of the Thunder King (quest).
Mogu'shan Vaults Guild Run is an achievement that is awarded for defeating all bosses in the Heart of Fear raid instance while in a guild group.
Hearth Defender's Axe is sold by at Stonehearth in Deepholm for .

The Heart of Y'Shaarj, a diseased, icy mass of flesh seething with Void energies, is the actual heart of the deceased Old God, Y'Shaarj. When Y'Shaarj was torn apart by the titan Aman'Thul, parts of the Old God's enormous body scattered across the landscape, and its monstrous heart was the largest part of it that remained intact. When Highkeeper Ra was on his way to Uldum to install the Forge of Origination, he came across the Heart of Y'Shaarj and decided to seal it in a vault below the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. "Heart of Pandaria" is the main theme of World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria, and was composed by Russell Brower.
The Heart of Gorgorek is found at the bottom of Cragplume Cauldron in Gorgrond during The Descent (quest). It is then transported to the Frostwall / Lunarfall garrison.

Heart of the Valorous was a buff that passively doubled Valor Points gains. It did not raise the weekly valor cap, so the long-term rate of Valor Point acquisition was unaffected. The buff was active on all characters during designated time windows, and persisted through death, logging out, and other interruptions until deactivated by Blizzard itself. With the removal of Valor Points in the Warlords of Draenor expansion, it is not expected to be seen again.
Heafty Salvaged Crates were sometimes rewarded after follower missions were completed.
Heart of the Fury was a quest item for Heart of the Fury (quest).

Heart-Lesion is an item level 483 death knight item set. It looks like the gear a death knight assembles by the end of their instanced starting experience.

Heartblood is a village in eastern Tanaan Jungle located near the . During the Assault on the Dark Portal, this was the first place the surviving champions from Azeroth fled after closing the Dark Portal. It contained a number of large cages containing draenei and Frostwolf prisoners, presumably for sacrifice at the Bleeding Altar to the east. Khadgar and his companions freed the slaves and burned down a number of huts in the village in order to slip through. After the Dark Portal's destruction any remaining Bleeding Hollow orcs left to other villages, like Zeth'Gol. The area is now populated by Bleeding Hollow Looters and Bleeding Hollow Scavengers.
A Headless Figurine is a Jewelcrafting skill-up item. Repairing it will yield either a Crude Gryphon Figurine or a Priceless Gryphon Figurine.
Heallix Skatterstorm is a goblin follower located at Frostwall in Frostfire Ridge. He can only be recruited using the Headhunter's Harvest from Frostwall Tavern.
The Heart of Azeroth is the shaman Class Hall in World of Warcraft: Legion, located at the Maelstrom.
Hearthglen Drudges are humanoid peons and peasants of the Argent Crusade found around the mine of Hearthglen, being afraid of what it contains. Some are also found inside Mardenholde Keep.
The Headpiece of the Shadow Council is a quest reward from The Nighthold: Lord of the Shadow Council.
The Headpiece of the Elunian Cycle a quest reward from Full Might of the Elves. This object has been in the possession of Tyrande Whisperwind since the War of the Ancients.
Healthy Dreamleaf is gathered from Dreamleaf in the Broken Isles.
The Heart of the Storm drops from the Wrath of Azshara in the Eye of Azshara.

__NOTOC__ The Heart of Dread is a large chamber in Darkheart Thicket. It is the last area of the dungeon. Cracks and fissures in the wood emanate the foul energy of the Emerald Nightmare. The Shade of Xavius is here, imprisoning Malfurion Stormrage and attempting to corrupt his mind. He is the last boss of the dungeon.
Headhunter Kuce'ba is a jungle troll located in Deliverance Point on the Broken Shore.

Heart of Nhal'athoth drops from Nhal'athoth at the Umbral Locus in Eredath. Upon defeating the demi-god, Alleria Windrunner absorbed its energies, resulting in the heart turning into a Remnant of Nhal'athoth.

The Heart-Shaped Carton appears in the bags of players below level 50 after killing Apothecary Hummel during Love is in the Air for the daily Looking For Dungeon quest. Level 50-60 players will instead be rewarded with the Heart-Shaped Box.
Hearthglen Mustangs are horses found at the stables of the Northridge Lumber Camp in Western Plaguelands.

Hearthglen Commanders are commanders found at Northridge Lumber Camp and Hearthglen in the Western Plaguelands. They lead patrols of Hearthglen Recruits.
Hearthglen Shieldbearers are humans found in Hearthglen and Taelan's Tower in the Western Plaguelands. The ones at the tower are found dead, seemingly killed by Redpine Looters.
The Headless Horseman's Hearthstone can be purchased from Tricky Treats vendors for during Hallow's End.
Healing Storm is a Retribution paladin artifact trait. It is linked to the Wrath of the Ashbringer trait.

Heart's ease is a flower that grows in Durotar after rain. It is similar to the spring's promise flowers of Kun-Lai Summit. According to Chen Stormstout, the trolls don't refer to the plant as "heart's ease" because they have noble hearts but do not think they should be at ease.
Heaping Handful of Damp Pollen is looted from Siren's Song in Kul Tiras and Zuldazar.
__NOTOC__ Heart-Lesion Helm is part of a set of equipment provided to Death Knight characters who used a Character Boost. The rare version of the item was looted from Big Crate of Salvage.
Headhunter Lee'za is a jungle troll located in the Rootway Collapse in Zuldazar.
A Healing Totem is summoned by Disciple of Halazzi in Dazar'alor.

The Hearth of Revelry is a vast feast hall located within the Halls of Valor. Here, members of the Valarjar eat and celebrate their accomplishments for all eternity. The hearth sits in the center of Odyn's halls, and all other sections can be accessed from here, including the Fields of the Eternal Hunt, the Seat of Ascension, and the High Gate.
Heart Guardians are sethrak located in the Atrium of Sethraliss in the Temple of Sethraliss. Upon their death, Energy Fragments appear.
Hearthbloom Petals are looted from Hearthblooms in the Crimson Forest in Drustvar.

Headhunter Gal'wana is a jungle troll located in Heart of the Empire in the Battle of Dazar'alor raid, in front of King Rastakhan acting as one of his bodyguards. He was most likely killed during the raid.

The Heart of Sethraliss is a sea serpent located in the Temple of Sethraliss.
Hearthblooms are plants found in the Crimson Forest in Drustvar.
